copy.theFoundationOfDebreZqalaMonasteryIsAnAn: Founded in the sixth century during the Aksumite era, Debre Ziquala Monastery is an ancient spiritual and historical landmark. It has long served as a center of Christianity, learning, and civilization in southern and central Ethiopia. In the fifteenth century, Italian cartographer Fra Mauro identified the monastery as a major landmark on his world map.
copy.theReConsecrationOfAbuneGebreSHolySpirit: Re-consecration by Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus
copy.inThe9thCenturyDuringTheReignOfJudithGud: During the ninth-century reign of Yodit Gudit, many spiritual treasures were destroyed, while Ziquala Debre Kewakibt Monastery, built by Emperor Gebre Meskel, remained concealed. The saint Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus later came to the mountain and re-consecrated the monastery. It grew stronger and expanded during the fifteenth-century reign of King Zera Yaqob.
copy.inThe16thCenturyTheMonasterySufferedGrea: The monastery suffered extensive damage during the sixteenth-century invasion of Ahmad Gragn and remained in ruins for about three centuries. It was rebuilt in the nineteenth century through the efforts of King Sahle Selassie of Shewa and Abba Gebre Hiwot. Churches built and restored during the reigns of Emperor Menelik and Empress Zewditu further enriched its architectural heritage.
copy.duringTheOccupationOfFascistItalyTheInva: During the Fascist Italian occupation, invading forces bombed the monastery and massacred its monks. Ziquala thus became a place of martyrdom and sacrifice for faith and country. During the Derg period, the monastery lost its landholdings, bringing further hardship to its monastic community.
copy.trustHistoryForTheNextGeneration: Entrusting a Living Heritage to the Next Generation
copy.debreZqalaMonasteryTransmitsThousandsOfY: Debre Ziquala Monastery connects a long inheritance of spiritual strength, love of country, and historical responsibility with modern education, passing that trust to the next generation. Today it continues to preserve its sacred character and history while serving as a beacon of learning.

overview.title: Ziquala Debre Kewakibt Communal Monastery
overview.body: Located 84 kilometers south of Addis Ababa and 40 kilometers from Bishoftu (Debre Zeit), the Ziquala Debre Kewakibt Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus Communal Monastery is a sacred spiritual sanctuary resting at an elevation of 2,989 meters above sea level. The monastery bears the name “Debre Kewakibt” (Mount of Stars) because its resident fathers and ascetics spend the entire night in unceasing prayer, shining spiritually like stars in the night sky.

spiritualLife.title: A Center of Traditional Learning, Prayer, and Stewardship
spiritualLife.body: Housing traditional ecclesiastical schools of liturgical reading (Nebab), Divine Liturgy (Qidase), sacred poetry (Qine), liturgical chant (Zema), and scriptural exegesis (Metshaf Tergwame), the monastery serves as a vital hub of scholarship, ascetic life, and community development. More than 300 monks and 160 nuns reside within the sanctuary, dedicating their lives to solitary contemplation, agriculture, traditional weaving, and prayer.

development.subtitle: Integrating spiritual ministry with social and economic development.
development.title: Self-Reliance & Sustainability Programs

oil.title: Edible Oil Processing Plant
oil.body: Established in Adulala town, the monastery’s oil processing plant serves as a vital economic resource for both the monastic community and neighboring residents.

school.title: Educational Institution
school.body: Founded in Bishoftu (Debre Zeit), our school fulfills the monastery's social responsibility by nurturing the next generation through holistic education and moral character.

mill.title: Community Grain Mill
mill.body: Situated within the monastery grounds, the grain mill provides essential daily milling services for both the monastic community and local villagers.

crafts.title: Artisanal Crafts & Traditional Weaving
crafts.body: Monastics handcraft traditional woven garments, liturgical textiles, and artisanal works to generate sustainable income for the monastery.

farming.title: Agriculture & Livestock Farming
farming.body: By carefully cultivating limited arable and grazing land, the monastery strives toward full food self-sufficiency.

legacy.title: A Pillar of Holiness and History
legacy.body: The Ziquala Debre Kewakibt Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus Communal Monastery stands as a sacred sanctuary of prayer for Ethiopians, an abode of saintly desert fathers, and an enduring pillar of holiness within the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church.

vision.title: Our School’s Vision
vision.body: To nurture citizens who can learn independently through participatory, student-centred teaching, uphold Ethiopian moral values, and contribute meaningfully to their country and community.

mission.title: Our School’s Mission
mission.body: To raise a generation of strong moral character by providing a modern, internationally informed curriculum rooted in Ethiopian identity and taught by qualified professionals.

values.subtitle: Spiritual, ethical, and educational values.
values.title: A Generation Grounded in Values
values.character: Raise citizens grounded in good character and human values.
values.faith: Nurture capable citizens guided by reverence for God.
values.learning: Combine spiritual wisdom with modern scientific knowledge in children’s education.
values.heritage: Cultivate respect for natural and human-made heritage.
values.skills: Develop knowledgeable, thoughtful, skilled, and capable citizens.

abbotMessage.title: Message of the Venerable Monastery Head
abbotMessage.body:
In the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one God. Amen.

Welcome to Ziquala Abo Monastery Kindergarten and Primary School. Our Ziquala Debre Kewakibt Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus Monastery established this school to nurture children and young people through modern scientific knowledge and spiritual wisdom.

Teachers and administrative staff selected for their professional competence and Christian moral character guide your children with care and wisdom.

socialResponsibility.title: Education for Everyone
socialResponsibility.body: Believing that quality education should be accessible to everyone, our school offers free educational opportunities to students from families in need. We also serve the wider community in partnership with public and private institutions.

purpose.name: Ziquala Abo Monastery Primary School
objectives: Help students grow with the moral character that distinguishes us as Ethiopians and that has been fading in recent times.
Raise a generation rich in knowledge, equipped with modern science and technology, and capable of bringing their country to the level of development the world has reached.

Help students grow with love for their country and fellow citizens, and with respect for natural and human-made heritage. Overall, help them develop well-rounded personalities in every respect—physically, psychologically, and socially—and grow with confidence in themselves.
purpose.vision: To see mature citizens who can teach themselves through participatory, student-centred learning, preserve good Ethiopian moral character, generate ideas, practices, and leadership that benefit their country and fellow citizens, and bring their country to the level of development the world has reached.
purpose.mission: Our mission is to provide excellent education through qualified professionals, supported by a modern, high-quality international curriculum that embraces Ethiopian identity, and to raise a morally grounded generation for whom working hard, both individually and together, is a way of life.
